analysis:
The PR only changes docs/architecture/inference.md. It adds a large "Context" section on the unregistered Nemotron Super local bridge, owner, image and text bindings, a local HTTP hook, MTP speculation, concurrency and prefill scheduling, and a resident recurrent prefix-checkpoint bank. It also edits the template-render-check text so multimodal fixtures run only when the "shared media discovery policy" accepts the config, replacing the old rule that `config.json` declares `vision_config`. That policy lives in model-registry.md and was not supplied.

Security-relevant claims: no model registration and no HTTP route in production, the hook is default-absent, ingress and media charges are applied before decode, only png/jpeg data URIs are accepted, and requests beyond the configured limit get 429.

One finding was reported (T-041/TB-007). The bank (`DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`) uses an unscoped local cache scope with no encryption or TTL, which conflicts with T-041's statements that production has no RAM tier and that cache scope is coordinator-authored per account.

No source code was supplied. The enforcement claims (media-before-decode charging, 429 behaviour, no production caller) are unverified and should be checked against NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache.swift, NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP and the registration paths.

findings.detail: The new inference.md text describes `NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache`. When `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, it gives the owner a resident recurrent checkpoint bank carved from the KV grant. Text requests are then submitted with prefix caching on and "the local unscoped cache scope". T-041 and its mitigations state that production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache. They also state that the only tier is the encrypted SSD tier, with a coordinator-authored per-account cacheSalt and a 30-minute TTL, and that SEC-035 sign-off is required for changes to the cache. The new bank has no per-account scope, no encryption and no TTL. If the Nemotron Super owner is ever registered or wired into ProviderLoop, concurrent consumers would share prefix state across tenants, with the TTFT oracle (leak #1) and no account isolation. The docs say the builder is unregistered and that no production caller installs the HTTP hook, so there is no live regression today. The threat model should record this path and gate it explicitly: either require a coordinator-supplied cacheSalt before registration, or extend T-041's affected files and detection_hint to cover `NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache` and the unscoped scope. The docs should also state that the env var is local/dev-only.
findings.title: Docs add a resident-RAM, unscoped prefix-cache path that contradicts T-041's "no production RAM tier" posture
